Review the following Rust code changes for Phase 1 of CODEFLOW — an AI code provenance system being added to the RTK project at `D:/code/invesments/tools_decisions/rtk-analysis/`.

## Context
RTK is a Rust CLI tool (105 .rs files, ~69K LOC) for filtering LLM token consumption. We're adding provenance tracking: who wrote code (AI vs human), content hashing, Ed25519 attestation, and a `blame` command.

## Files changed (modified)
- `Cargo.toml` — added prost, ed25519-dalek, blake3, rand, hex deps
- `build.rs` — added prost-build proto compilation + fixed MinGW stack flag
- `src/core/mod.rs` — added new module exports with #[allow(dead_code)]
- `src/cmds/mod.rs` — added codeflow module
- `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — added provenance capture on PreToolUse
- `src/main.rs` — added Blame command variant and dispatch

## Files created
- `proto/events.proto` — protobuf schema (7 event types)
- `src/core/proto.rs` — includes generated proto code
- `src/core/content_hash.rs` — blake3 content hashing (5 tests)
- `src/core/attestation.rs` — Ed25519 key management (5 tests)
- `src/core/provenance.rs` — ProvenanceRecord + SQLite store (6 tests)
- `src/core/agent_trace.rs` — Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export (2 tests)
- `src/cmds/codeflow/mod.rs` — codeflow command module
- `src/cmds/codeflow/blame_cmd.rs` — blame command implementation

## Acceptance criteria
1. Proto schema compiles with prost-build
2. Ed25519 keypair auto-generated, persisted at dirs::data_dir()/rtk/keys/
3. ProvenanceRecord created for file changes via diff-on-next-PreToolUse pattern
4. `rtk blame <file>` shows line-by-line AI attribution
5. Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export
6. Hook latency remains <5ms (fail-open)
7. No regression on existing 2012 tests
8. 15+ new tests

## Review focus
- Security: Ed25519 key handling, SQLite injection, fail-open safety
- Correctness: diff-on-next-PreToolUse pattern, snapshot consistency
- Performance: hook latency (each invocation is a separate OS process)
- Existing code patterns: does new code follow RTK conventions?
- No regressions to existing business logic

Read all changed/created files and provide findings.

1165	fn run_fallback(parse_error: clap::Error) -> Result<i32> {
1166	    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
1167	
1168	    // No args → show Clap's error (user ran just "rtk" with bad syntax)
1169	    if args.is_empty() {
1170	        parse_error.exit();
1171	    }
1172	
1173	    // RTK meta-commands should never fall back to raw execution.
1174	    // e.g. `rtk gain --badtypo` should show Clap's error, not try to run `gain` from $PATH.
1175	    if RTK_META_COMMANDS.contains(&args[0].as_str()) {
1176	        parse_error.exit();
1177	    }
1178	
1179	    let raw_command = args.join(" ");
1180	    let error_message = core::utils::strip_ansi(&parse_error.to_string());
1181	
1182	    // Start timer before execution to capture actual command runtime
1183	    let timer = core::tracking::TimedExecution::start();
1184	
1185	    // TOML filter lookup — bypass with RTK_NO_TOML=1
1186	    // Use basename of args[0] so absolute paths (/usr/bin/make) still match "^make\b".
1187	    let lookup_cmd = {
1188	        let base = std::path::Path::new(&args[0])
1189	            .file_name()
1190	            .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
1191	            .unwrap_or_else(|| args[0].clone());
1192	        std::iter::once(base.as_str())
1193	            .chain(args[1..].iter().map(|s| s.as_str()))
1194	            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
1195	            .join(" ")
1196	    };
1197	    let toml_match = if std::env::var("RTK_NO_TOML").ok().as_deref() == Some("1") {
1198	        None
1199	    } else {
1200	        core::toml_filter::find_matching_filter(&lookup_cmd)
1201	    };
1202	
1203	    if let Some(filter) = toml_match {
1204	        // TOML match: capture stdout for filtering
1205	        let result = if filter.filter_stderr {
1206	            // Merge stderr into stdout so the filter can strip banners emitted by tools like liquibase
1207	            core::utils::resolved_command(&args[0])
1208	                .args(&args[1..])
1209	                .stdin(std::process::Stdio::inherit())
1210	                .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())
1211	                .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped()) // captured for merging
1212	                .output()
1213	        } else {
1214	            core::utils::resolved_command(&args[0])
1215	                .args(&args[1..])
1216	                .stdin(std::process::Stdio::inherit())
1217	                .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped()) // capture
1218	                .stderr(std::process::Stdio::inherit()) // stderr always direct
1219	                .output()
1220	        };
1221	
1222	        match result {
1223	            Ok(output) => {
1224	                let exit_code = core::utils::exit_code_from_output(&output, &raw_command);
1225	                let stdout_raw = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
1226	                let stderr_raw = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
1227	
1228	                // Merge stderr into the text to filter when filter_stderr is enabled;
1229	                // otherwise emit stderr directly so it is always visible.
1230	                let combined_raw = if filter.filter_stderr {
1231	                    format!("{}{}", stdout_raw, stderr_raw)
1232	                } else {
1233	                    stdout_raw.to_string()
1234	                };
1235	                // Tee raw output BEFORE filtering on failure — lets LLM re-read if needed
1236	                let tee_hint = if !output.status.success() {
1237	                    core::tee::tee_and_hint(&combined_raw, &raw_command, exit_code)
1238	                } else {
1239	                    None
1240	                };
1241	
1242	                let filtered = core::toml_filter::apply_filter(filter, &combined_raw);
1243	                println!("{}", filtered);
1244	                if let Some(hint) = tee_hint {
1245	                    println!("{}", hint);
1246	                }
1247	
1248	                timer.track(
1249	                    &raw_command,
1250	                    &format!("rtk:toml {}", raw_command),
1251	                    &combined_raw,
1252	                    &filtered,
1253	                );
1254	                core::tracking::record_parse_failure_silent(&raw_command, &error_message, true);
1255	
1256	                Ok(exit_code)
1257	            }
1258	            Err(e) => {
1259	                // Command not found — same behaviour as no-TOML path
1260	                core::tracking::record_parse_failure_silent(&raw_command, &error_message, false);
1261	                eprintln!("[rtk: {}]", e);
1262	                Ok(127)
1263	            }
1264	        }
1265	    } else {
1266	        // No TOML match: original passthrough behaviour (Stdio::inherit, streaming)
1267	        let status = core::utils::resolved_command(&args[0])
1268	            .args(&args[1..])
1269	            .stdin(std::process::Stdio::inherit())
1270	            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::inherit())
1271	            .stderr(std::process::Stdio::inherit())
1272	            .status();
1273	
1274	        match status {
1275	            Ok(s) => {
1276	                timer.track_passthrough(&raw_command, &format!("rtk fallback: {}", raw_command));
1277	
1278	                core::tracking::record_parse_failure_silent(&raw_command, &error_message, true);
1279	
1280	                Ok(core::utils::exit_code_from_status(&s, &raw_command))
1281	            }
1282	            Err(e) => {
1283	                core::tracking::record_parse_failure_silent(&raw_command, &error_message, false);
1284	                // Command not found or other OS error — single message, no duplicate Clap error
1285	                eprintln!("[rtk: {}]", e);
1286	                Ok(127)
1287	            }
1288	        }
1289	    }
1290	}

Now I have enough information for a comprehensive review.

## Code Review Summary

### Scope
- Files: 14 (6 modified, 8 created)
- LOC added: ~900 (new modules) + ~90 (hook integration) + ~40 (main.rs dispatch)
- Focus: Security, correctness, performance, convention adherence

### Overall Assessment
Solid Phase 1 implementation. The code follows RTK patterns well (fail-open, `writeln!` to stdout, parameterized SQL, `best_effort` wrappers). The diff-on-next-PreToolUse pattern is sound for a per-process-invocation model. There are several issues ranging from a critical security gap to medium-priority correctness concerns.

---

### Critical Issues

**C1. Ed25519 private key has no file permission protection on Windows** (`attestation.rs:83-88`)

The `#[cfg(unix)]` block sets `chmod 600` on the key file, but Windows has no equivalent protection. The key is written world-readable. On multi-user Windows machines (CI agents, shared dev boxes), any user can read the signing key and forge attestations.

Impact: Attestation integrity is meaningless on Windows if an attacker reads the key.

Fix: Use Windows ACL APIs via the `windows` crate or `icacls` to restrict to owner-only. At minimum, document the limitation. Alternatively, consider Windows DPAPI for key-at-rest protection.

```rust
#[cfg(windows)]
{
    // Use icacls to restrict access (best-effort)
    let _ = std::process::Command::new("icacls")
        .args([key_file.to_str().unwrap_or_default(), "/inheritance:r", "/grant:r", &format!("{}:F", whoami())])
        .output();
}
```

**C2. `truncate_str` slices on byte boundary, will panic on multi-byte UTF-8** (`blame_cmd.rs:86-92`)

`&s[..max - 3]` indexes bytes, not chars. If a model_id or timestamp contains non-ASCII characters (e.g., from user-controlled `developer_id`), this panics at runtime.

Fix:
```rust
fn truncate_str(s: &str, max: usize) -> String {
    if s.len() <= max {
        s.to_string()
    } else {
        let boundary = s.char_indices()
            .take_while(|(i, _)| *i <= max - 3)
            .last()
            .map(|(i, c)| i + c.len_utf8())
            .unwrap_or(0);
        format!("{}...", &s[..boundary])
    }
}
```

---

### High Priority

**H1. Snapshot `INSERT OR REPLACE` without UNIQUE constraint causes unbounded row growth** (`provenance.rs:113-124, 235-239`)

The `provenance_snapshots` table uses `INSERT OR REPLACE` on `(file_path, content_hash, timestamp)`, but `file_path` has no UNIQUE constraint. `INSERT OR REPLACE` without a UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY constraint that triggers a conflict always INSERTs -- it never replaces. Every snapshot call appends a new row. Over time, `get_snapshot` returns the first match (non-deterministic without ORDER BY), and the table grows without bound.

Fix: Add `UNIQUE(file_path)` to the snapshot table:
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS provenance_snapshots (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    file_path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    content_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    timestamp TEXT NOT NULL
)
```

**H2. `collect_tracked_files` shells out to `git ls-files` on every hook invocation** (`hook_cmd.rs:618-650`)

Each PreToolUse hook is a separate OS process. `git ls-files` on a large repo can take 50-200ms, violating the <5ms latency target. For a repo with 10K tracked files, the subsequent blake3 hash loop adds more.

Impact: Hook latency far exceeds 5ms budget on non-trivial repos.

Mitigation options:
1. Cache file list in SQLite with a TTL (e.g., 30s)
2. Only hash files in `git diff --name-only` (changed files since last commit)
3. Skip provenance capture when `RTK_PROVENANCE=0` (opt-out) -- already partially there via `best_effort`, but the latency cost is paid before the error

**H3. `capture_provenance` hashes every tracked source file on every hook call** (`hook_cmd.rs:577-609`)

Even with `collect_tracked_files` returning results, the loop hashes every file and queries SQLite for each one. On a project with 500 source files, that is 500 blake3 hashes + 500 SQLite SELECT queries per hook invocation.

Fix: Use file mtime as a cheap pre-filter. Only hash files whose mtime changed since last check. Or batch the SQLite snapshot lookups into a single `WHERE file_path IN (...)` query.

**H4. `Blame` command not added to `is_operational_command` or `RTK_META_COMMANDS`** (`main.rs:2522-2568, 1146-1163`)

The new `Blame` command is not listed in `is_operational_command()` (no integrity check) and not in `RTK_META_COMMANDS` (so bad flags fall through to raw execution instead of showing Clap errors). This is inconsistent -- Blame is a meta/query command like `gain` or `discover`.

Fix: Add `"blame"` to `RTK_META_COMMANDS`.

### Medium Priority

**M1. TOCTOU race in `load_or_generate`** (`attestation.rs:64-91`)

`key_file.exists()` check followed by `fs::read` or `fs::create_dir_all` + `fs::write` has a race window. Two concurrent RTK processes (common with multiple hook invocations) could both see `exists() == false`, both generate keys, and one overwrites the other. The loser's provenance records are signed with a key that no longer exists on disk.

Severity: Medium in practice (first-run only), but could cause verification failures.

Fix: Use `OpenOptions::create_new(true)` which atomically creates-or-fails:
```rust
match fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true).open(&key_file) {
    Ok(mut f) => { /* write key */ },
    Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists => { /* read existing */ },
    Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),
}
```

**M2. `std::mem::forget(dir)` in test causes temp directory leak** (`provenance.rs:321`)

`std::mem::forget(dir)` prevents the `TempDir` destructor from cleaning up. This leaks a directory per test run. Use `dir.into_path()` if you need the path to outlive the `TempDir`, or restructure the test to keep `dir` alive.

**M3. `ContributorType::from_str` shadows the trait `std::str::FromStr`** (`provenance.rs:49-56`)

This is an inherent method named `from_str` which shadows the standard trait. If anyone tries to use `"ai".parse::<ContributorType>()` it won't work. Consider implementing `FromStr` trait instead, or rename to `from_label`.

**M4. `session_id` extraction from hook payload is fragile** (`hook_cmd.rs:398-403`)

The Claude hook JSON may not contain `session_id`. When absent, it defaults to `"unknown"`, which means all provenance records from unidentified sessions share the same session ID. This makes `query_by_session("unknown")` return unrelated records.

**M5. `#[allow(dead_code)]` on all new modules** (`core/mod.rs:19-26`)

All four new modules are annotated with `#[allow(dead_code)]`. While `content_hash`, `provenance`, and `agent_trace` ARE used from `hook_cmd.rs` and `blame_cmd.rs`, the `#[allow(dead_code)]` hides genuine unused code warnings (e.g., `hash_diff`, `hash_file` if unused outside tests). Remove the blanket allow and apply it only to specific items that are intentionally reserved for future use.

**M6. Proto module (`proto.rs`) is declared but never used** (`core/mod.rs:18`)

The `proto` module exists and compiles the protobuf definitions, but no code actually uses the generated types. The proto schema defines `EventEnvelope`, `CostEvent`, `GovernanceEvent`, `QualityEvent` -- none of which are referenced anywhere. This adds ~2s to first build for prost-build compilation with zero runtime benefit in Phase 1.

### Low Priority

**L1. `hash_diff` function is arguably misleading** (`content_hash.rs:14-17`)

It concatenates old and new with a newline separator, but this is order-dependent and collision-prone if either string contains newlines. Not currently used outside tests, but the API shape could mislead future callers.

**L2. `run_enrich` exposed as public API but no CLI test** (`blame_cmd.rs:94-99`)

The enrichment path (`rtk blame --enrich --model <id> <file>`) has no integration test. The `session` param in the CLI is positionally the `file` argument, which is confusing semantics.

**L3. `rand = "0.8"` may conflict with `ed25519-dalek`'s `rand_core` dependency** (`Cargo.toml:41`)

ed25519-dalek 2.x uses rand_core 0.6. rand 0.8 also uses rand_core 0.6, so this works, but rand 0.9 (which may resolve depending on other deps) uses rand_core 0.9 and would break. Pin to `rand = "0.8"` explicitly or use `rand_core` directly since only `OsRng` is needed.
